Quality gate, fast (lint, tests, drift checks)
Quality gate, full (adds mypy strict and the production deploy check)

convention_files.becomes: Django models. Tenant data subclasses OrganizationScopedModel.
Business rules, one implementation shared by REST viewsets and actions.
@action functions: REST /api/v1/actions/<name>/, MCP tool, CLI, Temporal activity.
@undo_handler functions that take back what a write action changed.
MCP resources (@mcp_resource) and prompts (@mcp_prompt) for AI agents.
register_event(...): webhook event types other systems can subscribe to.
personal(...) / not_personal(...): the data catalog entry for every model (LGPD).
declare_setting(key, type, default, description): typed settings an operator can override.
@job: cron-style maintenance, run by Temporal Schedules or run_scheduler.
Classic DRF viewsets, only when a plain CRUD resource is wanted besides actions.

definition_of_done: python scripts/verify.py passes (use --fast while iterating, the full gate before you stop).
New model: classified in <app>/privacy.py; tenant data subclasses OrganizationScopedModel.
New action: docstring written for a model reader, a scope, write/destructive/undoable declared, input and output are pydantic models.
Generated files are fresh: actions_catalog, check_openapi.py --write, gen_docs.py.
A test covers the new behaviour, including a cross-tenant attempt and a read-only role.
Docs updated in docs/en and docs/pt-BR; the CHANGELOG has a line for anything a user sees.
No secret, personal data or production detail appears in code, tests, logs or messages.
forbidden: Model.objects in actions.py or agent.py (use ctx.scoped / ctx.get).
except Exception: pass, or catching an error only to silence a failing test.
Logging request bodies, tokens, e-mail addresses or documents.
csrf_exempt without a written reason, raw SQL built with f-strings, eval, pickle.
Editing generated files (docs/reference/*, openapi-schema.yml, AGENTS.md) by hand.
Storing an API key, token or secret in clear (hash it, or encrypt it with the key ring).

lgpd_decisions.answer: Yes: personal(...). No: not_personal(model, 'why'), and be ready to defend the reason.
lgpd_decisions.question: Does a row relate to a person (directly or by a key that can be traced back)?

lgpd_decisions.answer: Category.IDENTIFIER, CONTACT, CREDENTIAL, FINANCIAL, LOCATION, BEHAVIOR, CONTENT, TECHNICAL, SENSITIVE (art. 5 II) or CHILD (art. 14). Sensitive and child fields must be encrypted.
lgpd_decisions.question: Which kind of data is each field?

lgpd_decisions.answer: resolver: by_user(Model, 'field'), by_subject(...), by_email_index(...); None only when rows cannot be tied to a person (the DPO then answers by hand).
lgpd_decisions.question: How is a person's row found?

lgpd_decisions.answer: purpose= a ProcessingPurpose code. Reuse a baseline one (account-and-access, product-content, security-and-audit, compliance-records) or add one in apps/privacy/baseline.py. Consent as the basis means a ConsentRecord chain and a withdrawal path.
lgpd_decisions.question: Why is it processed, and on what legal basis?

lgpd_decisions.answer: on_erase='delete', 'anonymize' (give the replacement values) or 'keep' (give the legal duty that requires it as reason=...).
lgpd_decisions.question: What happens on erasure?

lgpd_decisions.answer: retention_field= the timestamp that starts the clock; the purpose's retention_days ends it.
lgpd_decisions.question: How long is it kept?

lgpd_decisions.answer: Mark the purpose involves_children and require guardian confirmation; see apps/privacy/age.py and docs/en/lgpd/overview.md (ECA Digital).
lgpd_decisions.question: Does it involve children?

lgpd_decisions.answer: Add a SubProcessor (country, transfer mechanism: LGPD art. 33, Res. CD/ANPD 19/2024).
lgpd_decisions.question: Does a new vendor see the data?

project.name: saas-django-backend
project.stack: Python 3.12+, Django 6.1, DRF, django-allauth (MFA), FastMCP, Temporal (optional), PostgreSQL, Redis, pydantic v2, structlog
project.summary: A security-first, LGPD-aware Django 6.1 foundation for a multi-tenant SaaS. One function declared with @action is a REST endpoint, an MCP tool, a Temporal activity and a CLI command at once.

rules.rule: Reach tenant rows only through ctx.scoped(Model) or ctx.get(Model, id). Never Model.objects (or _default_manager) in actions.py, actions/*.py or agent.py.
rules.why: A forgotten organization filter is a cross-tenant leak (IDOR).

rules.enforced_by: tests/test_tenancy_structure.py (every organization column is scoped or explained)
rules.rule: A model that holds tenant data subclasses apps.organizations.models.OrganizationScopedModel.
rules.why: It carries the organization foreign key the scoped helpers filter on.

rules.rule: Put business rules in services.py. Actions and viewsets only translate input and output.
rules.why: REST, MCP, CLI and Temporal then cannot disagree about a rule.

rules.enforced_by: import-time check in apps.actions.registry and tests/test_conformance.py
rules.rule: A write action declares undoable=True (and records the change with ctx.record_change plus a handler in undo.py) or undoable='<why it cannot be undone>'. It also calls ctx.set_target(row) so the audit event names the record.
rules.why: An agent that changes data must be able to take the change back, or say it cannot.

rules.enforced_by: apps.common.exceptions, mask_error_details in the MCP server
rules.rule: Refuse with a DomainError subclass (NotFound, Forbidden, Invalid, Conflict) and a message written for the caller. Let anything else propagate as a bug.
rules.why: Django ValidationError text and ORM errors must not reach clients (they are masked).

rules.rule: Every model is declared in <app>/privacy.py: personal(model, resolver=..., fields={...}, purpose=..., on_erase=...) or not_personal(model, 'why').
rules.why: Export, erasure, retention and the RoPA are generated from the catalog (LGPD art. 18, 37).

rules.rule: List every field that holds data about a person (e-mail, phone, document, address, name, ip, user agent) in personal(fields=...). Sensitive and child data are EncryptedTextField.
rules.why: An unlisted field is skipped by export and erasure.

rules.rule: Use EncryptedTextField for free text that can contain personal data, and blind_index() for equality lookups on it. Never filter on an encrypted column.
rules.why: A database dump or a replica must not expose what people wrote.

rules.rule: Never put credentials, tokens or personal data in logs, audit metadata, action outputs or error messages. Audit metadata keys are snake_case ids and counts.
rules.why: Logs, traces and the audit trail outlive the data (LGPD art. 46).

rules.rule: Call a URL somebody else chose only through apps.common.netguard. Never requests/httpx directly with a user-supplied URL.
rules.why: SSRF: the server would otherwise reach the cloud metadata service or the private network.

rules.rule: register_event(...) in events.py and emit(...) inside the same transaction, with ids only in the payload.
rules.why: The outbox delivers after commit; receivers fetch documents through the API.

rules.rule: Workflow code holds no Django ORM and no I/O; it calls actions through apps.flows.sdk.call_action. Activities are sync functions.
Add configuration with env_str/env_int/env_bool/env_list in config/settings/*.py, with a comment above it. Production-only constraints go in config/settings/validators.py.
rules.why: The environment-variable reference is generated from these calls.

rules.rule: A resource a tenant can create without bound checks apps.organizations.quotas.
rules.why: One tenant must not be able to fill the database or the bucket for all.

rules.rule: No inline scripts or styles and no third-party origins on shipped pages (script-src and style-src are 'self').
rules.why: The Content-Security-Policy is the second line of defence against injected script.

rules.rule: Never edit a migration that has shipped. Add a new one; keep data migrations idempotent.
rules.why: Other databases already applied the old one.

rules.rule: Every page under docs/en has a twin under docs/pt-BR. Generated references come from scripts/gen_docs.py; do not edit them by hand.
rules.why: The platform is documented for Brazilian teams first.

rules.rule: Do not loosen a production validator, widen CORS, set NETGUARD_ALLOW_PRIVATE or DEBUG outside local settings, or catch and swallow an exception to make a test pass.
rules.why: These are the controls the threat model relies on (docs/en/security/threat-model.md).
